summary: A dry run must not perform the --deliver side effect (file write or webhook POST); delivery is gated on !flags.dryRun and the delivery buffer is not even allocated.
reason: The post-run hook delivered the captured output buffer after every successful command, so '--dry-run --deliver file:...' wrote a file and '--dry-run --deliver webhook:...' sent a POST. --dry-run promises to show the request without sending, and --deliver is exactly the kind of external side effect that promise covers. A dry run also no longer captures an output buffer that would only be discarded.
validated_outcome: go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestDeliverCapturedOutputRespectsDryRun passes (file sink not written, webhook sink not dialed, real run still delivers byte-for-byte).
